chunks: Do not take an old, decrepit, broken-limbed, sick or unsound animal.
Do not entrust the animals (for custody) except to one whom you trust to take care of Muslims’ property till he hands it over to their chief who will distribute it.

Do not entrust it to anyone except he who is a well wisher, God-fearing, trustworthy and watchful, and who is not harsh on Muslims’ property, nor makes them run too much, nor tires them, nor labours them.
Then send to us all that you have collected and we shall deal with it as Allāh has ordered.
ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for selecting trustworthy custodians for Islamic tax assets?
ai.summary: This directive from Imam Ali (AS) outlines the rigorous standards for selecting tax collectors, emphasizing piety, trustworthiness, and gentleness to prevent exploitation of the Muslim community. It reflects the Shia understanding of just governance, where the Imam acts as the ultimate custodian of public wealth, ensuring that resources like khums and zakat are distributed according to divine decree rather than administrative convenience.
